Armitage Auctions, Invermay. Closing Wed 30 Sep 2026

Sleeper tracker

Auctions 1 and 2 have full market passes; auction 3 has first-pass research and its market pass is still running. Each lot shows sold prices, unsold results and asking prices separately, and only sold prices set a maximum bid. The most solid evidence: the 1964 Macallan (lot 768, four sold results, bid heavily contested), the Ebatarinja watercolour (lot 62), the Perth Mint gold and silver Federation coin (lot 876, one verified sale of A$1,000 hammer), Cardhu 2020 (lot 677) and the Tiffany bangle (lot 849). Many lots are already bid at or past their ceilings, and the cards say so. Wine has almost no sold data, only asking prices. Bids move fast near the close, so check them before you act.

Only 2 of the titles say the statue is included, and completeness and the game code are unverified, so this cannot be High.

Comps dropped: None dropped. I opened the PriceCharting page and all 6 prices and dates match what the valuer claimed. I re-ranked 4 of them as 'probable' because their titles do not mention the statue. I did not use the valuer's AUD 1.50 rate. A live rate (open.er-api.com, 29 Sep 2026) is AUD 1.425, so every AUD figure is about 5% lower than the valuer's. Sales left out: game or steelbook-only sales (USD 5 to 45), a used-code sale (USD 45.42), a statue-only sale (USD 53.69) and the sealed/new sales.

Working: Rate: USD 1 = AUD 1.425. Comps in AUD: 188.76, 221.17, 207.39, 200.57, 166.31, 162.35. The median is about 194 to 201. likely_resale = AUD 190, rounded down because contents and the game code are unverified. The Heroes VII set is ignored as a small upside. Fees: eBay AU about 13.5% x 190 = 25.65. Outbound postage for the bulky box, sent free, is about AUD 35. net_resale = 190 - 25.65 - 35 = 129.35. FLIP max hammer = 129.35 / 2.44 = 53.01, rounded down to 50. Check: 50 x 1.22 = 61 all-in. KEEP max hammer = lowest clear same-item comp AUD 162.35 / 1.22 = 133.07, rounded down to 130. Check: 130 x 1.22 = 158.60 all-in. The valuer had 55 and 140 because of the higher exchange rate. The current bid is $30, so the FLIP figure is still in reach.
